item.title: Trump Quiet as Europe Slams Israeli West Bank Settlements
item.description: Sanctions over settlements have so far failed to provoke the US president’s ire.
item.dc:creator: Dan Williams

item.title: TPS Changes Have El Salvador Immigrants Facing Trump Deportation Push
item.description: Losing temporary protected status means Salvadorans must return to a country many of them no longer recognize or go underground in the US.
item.dc:creator: Nacha Cattan and Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Why Data Center Backlash Is Shaping the 2026 US Midterm Elections
item.description: Spending on data centers, the backbone of the artificial intelligence industry, has reached new highs in 2026. In response to the infrastructure boom, opposition to the facilities has exploded this year, escalating from a niche local issue to a defining topic ahead of the November midterm elections. Almost overnight, candidates across the political spectrum have reshaped their messaging in response to a grassroots backlash against a build-out backed by hundreds of billions of dollars in tech spe
item.dc:creator: Emily Birnbaum

item.title: Spain's Albares Says Foused on Returning to Normality in Ceuta
item.description: Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares discusses the late-July incident that saw roughly 80,000 people illegally enter Ceuta, Spain’s exclave in North Africa, from Morocco. "We are focused on giving back normality," Albares tells Bloomberg Television. "We are totally in favor of understanding everything," he says, stressing that there were several ongoing probes. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Hits Several Iran Oil Tankers in Response to Warship Attack
item.description: The US attacked more Iranian oil tankers overnight, with the worsening tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz sending Brent crude beyond $100 a barrel.
item.dc:creator: Arsalan Shahla and Kate Sullivan

item.title: Colombia’s Radical Austerity Plan Faces a Tough Road in Congress
item.description: Facing what it calls the biggest fiscal crisis since Colombian independence two centuries ago, the government of President Abelardo de la Espriella is doing everything it can to avoid raising taxes.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: Spain Must ‘Rethink’ Morocco Ties, Foreign Minister Says
item.description: Spain must overhaul its relationship with Morocco following a surge of migrants into Ceuta, the country’s north African exclave, Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares said — even as he stopped short of blaming Rabat for the incident.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro, Jorge Valero and Francine Lacqua

item.title: Iran Accuses the US of Using Nuclear Watchdog to Justify Strikes
item.description: Iran accused the US and Israel of cloaking military strikes against its nuclear facilities beneath the legal authority wielded by inspectors at the United Nations nuclear watchdog.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Merz Attacks Far Right for Russia Stance, ‘Ethnic Cleansing’
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz lashed out at the far-right Alternative for Germany for its embrace of Russia and migration aims that he said amount to “ethnic cleansing” as the government grapples with the fallout from the party’s election win this week.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber and Arne Delfs

item.title: Brent Oil at $100 for First Time Since July
item.description: Brent oil hit $100 a barrel for the first time since July as attacks between the US and Iran and a recovery in Chinese oil buying propelled the global crude benchmark higher. US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers carrying crude oil on Tuesday in response to two attempts to hit a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles in as many days, Central Command said. Bloomberg's Stephen Stapczynski reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Says It Destroyed Iran Tankers After Navy Ship Targeted | Daybreak Europe 9/9/2026
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers carrying crude oil on Tuesday in response to two attempts to hit a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles in as many days, Central Command said.
Plus, the US escalated its trade war with Canada following Ottawa’s tariff retaliation, moving to block imports of some products while slapping new tariffs on others, as well as seeking to bar Canadian companies from selling to government contractors.
Today's guests: Mike Parra, DHL Express Europe, CEO; Antoine Flamarion, Tikehau Capital Co-founder. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Serb Strongman Calls Snap Election Echoing Putin’s Power Move
item.description: Serbia will hold a snap vote on Oct. 25, setting in motion a political playbook that may see the embattled President Aleksandar Vucic transition to the role of prime minister.
item.dc:creator: Misha Savic

item.title: US Escalates Trade War With Canada
item.description: The US escalated its trade war with Canada following Ottawa’s tariff retaliation. Washington moved to block imports of some products while placing new tariffs on others, as well as seeking to bar Canadian companies from selling to government contractors. Bloomberg's Rosalind Mathieson reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Have Some Shame': Philippine Defense Chief Slams China on Stage
item.description:
The Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. hit out at China after a memo asserting Beijing’s position over their longstanding maritime dispute was delivered to him while he was onstage at an international forum in Seoul.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Prices Closer to $100 After US Attacks Iranian Tankers
item.description: US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers carrying crude oil on Tuesday following two attempts to hit a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles in as many days, Central Command said. Brent oil moved closer to $100 a barrel after the US struck Iranian tankers near the Kharg Island export hub and in the Gulf of Oman. Bloomberg’s Onur Ant and Clara Ferreira Marques break down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Najib Said to Seek 1MDB Pardon as Anwar’s Coalition Resists
item.description: Malaysia’s jailed former premier Najib Razak is seeking another royal intervention in his corruption conviction linked to the multibillion dollar 1MDB scandal, according to people familiar with the matter, a move that’s drawn opposition from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s coalition.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan, Niluksi Koswanage and Ram Anand

item.title: Key New Hampshire Senate Race to Pit Pappas Against Sununu
item.description: Representative Chris Pappas fought off a progressive challenge to win the Democratic primary for a New Hampshire Senate seat, AP and NBC projected, setting up a November showdown with former Republican Senator John Sununu.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ryan

item.title: UK, France and Canada Hit Israeli Settlements With Sanctions
item.description: The UK, France, Canada and other countries announced coordinated measures against Israeli settlements in the West Bank, as western nations sought to raise pressure on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Dan Williams

item.title: Europe to Send Kyiv US Air Defenses for Russian Winter Blitz
item.description: European countries will buy Ukraine more US-made Patriot air defense systems and send missiles from their own stocks to help Ukraine repel an expected Russian winter onslaught.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Andrea Palasciano and Michael Nienaber

item.title: ‘Have Some Shame’: Philippines Slams China After Memo Mishap
item.description: Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. hit out at China at an international forum after a memo asserting Beijing’s position over their longstanding maritime dispute was delivered to him while he was speaking onstage.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi
